fact: The consolidated text of the Cybercrimes Act (Cap. 443, Revised Edition 2023, originally Act No. 14 of 2015) states it commenced on 1 September 2015 under GN No. 528 of 2015 and applies to Mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar, criminalising illegal access, interception, data interference, fraud and forgery.

The ICT Minister said on 19 August 2026 that section 29 of the Cybercrimes Act provides a fine of not less than 100m/- or three times the damage, imprisonment of at least five years, or both, for damaging critical ICT infrastructure.

FB Attorneys describes Tanzania's Cybercrimes Act as criminalising false or misleading published information (section 16) and cyberbullying (section 23), and setting a take-down notification procedure (section 45).
Clyde & Co lists the Cybercrimes Act, Chapter 443 Revised Edition 2023, among the laws that may apply to AI use in Tanzania.
The ICT minister told the National Assembly that the ministry is starting a review of the Cybercrime Act of 2015, which implies it is in force.

Government Notice No. 147, published 19 June 2026, is an Order made under section 28 of the Cybercrimes Act (Cap. 443) that sets duties on owners of designated critical information infrastructure, showing the Act is in force.
